items.stem: The maximum number of canonical correlations for sets of sizes p and q is:
items.explanation: A p×q standardized cross block has rank at most min(p,q).

items.stem: The first canonical correlation is the maximum correlation between:
options: two linear combinations, one from each set
items.explanation: Canonical correlation optimises weights for both variable sets and maximises the correlation of the resulting composites.

items.stem: The block Σ₁₂ in a joint covariance partition contains:
items.explanation: Σ₁₂ contains covariances between each variable in X and each variable in Y.

items.stem: The singular values of C=Σ₁₁⁻¹/²Σ₁₂Σ₂₂⁻¹/² are:
items.explanation: The singular values of the standardized cross-covariance matrix are canonical correlations.

items.stem: If C′C has largest eigenvalue .81, the largest canonical correlation is:
items.explanation: Take the square root of the largest eigenvalue: √.81=.90.

items.stem: If Σ₁₁=I and Σ₂₂=I, C equals:
items.explanation: Both inverse square-root factors are identity matrices, so C=Σ₁₂.

items.stem: For p=3 and q=2, the maximum number of nonzero roots is:
items.explanation: The rank of a 3×2 matrix cannot exceed two.

items.stem: If squared roots are .49 and .16, the largest canonical correlation is:
items.explanation: The largest squared root is .49, so the correlation is √.49=.70.

items.stem: The dimensions of C are:
items.explanation: The product of a p×p matrix, p×q matrix and q×q matrix has dimensions p×q.

items.stem: Subsequent canonical pairs are:
options: uncorrelated with earlier canonical variates within each set
items.explanation: Later pairs are constrained to be uncorrelated with earlier canonical variates and cannot exceed the first correlation.

items.stem: If Σ₁₁=diag(4,1), Σ₂₂=diag(1,9), Σ₁₂=I₂, the first canonical correlation is:
items.explanation: Standardisation gives C=diag(1/2,1/3); the largest singular value is 1/2.

items.stem: Which statements are correct?
items.explanation: The first three statements are true. Canonical correlation need not equal any one raw pairwise correlation.
statements: The first pair maximises correlation between two composites.
Canonical correlations are between zero and one.
There are at most min(p,q) nonzero roots.
A canonical correlation must equal one raw pairwise correlation.

A.why: The first pair is defined by maximising over admissible weights.

B.why: They are singular values of a valid standardized cross-covariance matrix.

C.why: The rank of a p×q matrix cannot exceed min(p,q).

D.why: Optimally weighted composites may have a correlation unlike any individual raw pair.

items.stem: Squared roots .36 and .04 give canonical correlations:
items.explanation: Take nonnegative square roots: .6 and .2.

items.stem: In a symmetric joint covariance matrix, Σ₂₁ equals:
items.explanation: The joint covariance matrix is symmetric, so the lower-left block is the transpose of the upper-right block.

items.stem: For C=diag(.6,.2), the largest canonical correlation is:
items.explanation: The singular values are the absolute diagonal entries; the largest is .60.

items.stem: If asked for the largest squared canonical correlation, report:
items.explanation: Eigenvalues of C′C are squared canonical correlations; do not take a square root when the squared value is requested.

items.stem: If the largest eigenvalue of C′C is .40, the maximum canonical correlation is approximately:
items.explanation: The maximum correlation is √.40≈.632.

items.stem: Which statements are correct for a standardized cross block C?
items.explanation: A, B and D are true; eigenvalues of C′C are squared correlations, not correlations.
statements: C′C and CC′ have the same nonzero eigenvalues.
Eigenvalues of C′C are canonical correlations themselves.
Canonical correlations are ordered from largest to smallest.

A.why: The standardized cross block retains p rows and q columns.

B.why: Both products share the nonzero squared singular values.

C.why: The nonnegative square roots of these eigenvalues are the canonical correlations.

D.why: The first canonical correlation is the maximum and roots are ordered downward.

items.stem: For a 2×2 C′C with trace .50 and determinant .04, larger eigenvalue .40, the maximum correlation is:
items.explanation: The largest canonical correlation is √.40≈.632.

items.stem: For June 2026 Q20 B=[[.5,0],[.3,.4]], which statements are true?
items.explanation: Trace=.50, determinant=.04, roots .40 and .10; maximum correlation is √.40≈.632.

A.why: The diagonal entries of B′B sum to .34+.16=.50.

C.why: .40 is the squared root; the correlation is √.40≈.632.

D.why: The smaller eigenvalue .10 gives the second correlation √.10≈.316.
